rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the full elution window without making the slope extremely steep or shallow. This should reveal whether any peaks are unretained, held to the final hold, or missing, which will guide narrowing the gradient window next.

All 10 compounds eluted well within the gradient, with the last peak corresponding to only about phi_e 0.38, so narrowing the gradient window should improve time efficiency while keeping all peaks in-gradient. Keeping tG and T fixed isolates the effect of the phi window and may sharpen selectivity around the tightest cluster near peaks 5–7.

The broad window at 0.95 was clearly better for time, and all pairs were already well resolved, so now test a steeper gradient to reduce run time further and see whether the critical 5–7 cluster remains comfortably separated. Comparing directly to injection 1 isolates slope sensitivity without changing the solvent window or temperature.

The critical cluster around peaks 5–7 is strongly slope-sensitive: tG 10 was too steep, while tG 20 was safely resolved but slower. An intermediate tG of 14 should recover enough resolution for the 5–7 region while likely keeping the run short enough to preserve or improve CRF.

The limiting pair 6–7 improved markedly from tG 10 to 14 and was fully resolved at tG 20, so a small increase to tG 16 should move that pair closer to baseline resolution while likely keeping the run short enough for a near-maximal score. This is the most direct refinement around the current best method.

At tG 14 the score is already excellent, and the main remaining opportunity is to improve the stubborn 6–7 pair without adding time; since slope helped only partially, a temperature shift is the next lever to test for selectivity changes. A modest drop to 35 C may alter that close pair enough while keeping the run comfortably short.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity by collapsing peaks 5–6, so test the opposite direction at the current best tG to see whether a modest increase improves the critical cluster without paying a time penalty. This directly probes whether temperature can outperform the 40 C optimum for the close mid-run group.

Temperature changes moved the critical cluster the wrong way, so 40 C appears best and the optimum likely lies between tG 14 and 16. Testing tG 12 maps the slope response more finely around the current best and helps confirm whether 14 is truly near-optimal or part of a broader ridge.

The broad 0.95 endpoint is fast, but all compounds elute by about phi_e 0.58, so trimming phi1 slightly may modestly flatten the gradient in the crowded mid-region without pushing the last peak too late. This tests whether a small narrowing of the window can improve the critical 6–7 separation while preserving the zero time penalty.

A small reduction of phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the score and the critical 6–7 pair while keeping no time penalty, suggesting the optimum may lie with a slightly narrower window. Testing 0.85 continues that trend cautiously to see if the crowded mid-region spreads a bit more before time cost appears.

Injection 9 is near-optimal, and reducing phi1 helped the critical pair without time penalty; now combine that narrower window with a slightly steeper gradient to see whether runtime can be trimmed while keeping the minimum resolution acceptably high. This tests whether the current optimum is driven more by window placement than by absolute gradient time.

The best region is clearly around phi1 0.90 and 40 C, and the critical 6–7 pair is still the limiter; increasing tG from 14 to 16 at this improved window should raise that pair toward full baseline resolution. This directly tests whether the gain in resolution outweighs any emerging time penalty better than at phi1 0.95.

Since phi1 0.90 at tG 14 is the best region and both 35 C and 45 C worsened the limiting pair, test a larger temperature shift downward to probe whether selectivity is nonmonotonic and may improve away from 40 C. This is a targeted check for a hidden temperature optimum before spending the remaining budget on finer solvent-window refinements.

Temperature exploration confirms 40 C is best, so return to the top method and test the other solvent-window edge: raising phi0 slightly should shift the crowded early-mid region to a somewhat shallower effective range without increasing gradient span. This may improve the persistent 6–7 separation while preserving the favorable runtime seen at phi1 0.90.

Raising phi0 to 0.10 improved the best method further, so combine that gain with the previously favorable reduction in phi1 to 0.85 to slightly narrow the window around the actual elution region. This may push the limiting 6–7 pair fully over the threshold while keeping runtime within the no-penalty zone.

The maximum CRF has already been reached, so this is a cautious robustness check one step narrower in phi1 to see whether the score remains at the cap with an even tighter window around the elution region. If it does, it offers a potentially more selective alternative while staying on the same proven tG and temperature.

The optimum appears to come from trimming the gradient window around the actual elution region, and increasing phi0 from 0.05 to 0.10 improved the score; one further step to 0.15 tests whether that trend continues without sacrificing the first peak to near-dead-time elution. This is the most informative remaining local refinement around the maximum-scoring method.

With phi0 0.15 the first peak is still retained but much earlier, and the method remains at the CRF ceiling, so one more upward step probes how far phi0 can be increased before the first compound becomes effectively unretained or selectivity deteriorates. This defines the robustness boundary while staying close to the current optimum region.

The best capped methods are now centered around phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, so test the nearby combination phi0 0.15/phi1 0.80 to map the plateau of optimal conditions and see whether the same maximum score persists with a slightly narrower upper bound. This refines the robust optimum region without changing the proven gradient time or temperature.

Since 0.10/0.85/14/40 is already at the CRF ceiling, the remaining value is to test whether the same optimized window tolerates a shorter gradient and could still achieve the cap. This directly checks the speed margin around the best solvent window while keeping temperature fixed at the proven optimum.

The capped optimum is robust at phi0 0.10–0.15 with phi1 0.85 and tG 14, so test whether the higher phi0 variant can better tolerate a shorter tG while maintaining full resolution. This explores the speed/resolution boundary of the best-performing window with one focused remaining slope check.

With the maximum already achieved, use a remaining injection to test robustness of the near-optimal solvent window to a temperature increase, since only phi0 0.05/phi1 0.95 at 45 C was explored before. This checks whether the improved window around 0.10–0.90 changes the temperature response of the critical pair.

The best method is already at the ceiling, but only its higher-temperature side was checked directly; test the lower-temperature side on the exact top-scoring solvent window to complete the local robustness picture. This verifies whether 40 C is truly the unique optimum at the winning composition or whether the capped performance persists nearby.

With two ceiling methods found, use one of the last injections to map the remaining adjacent corner of the local optimum region by combining the successful higher phi0 with the slightly higher phi1. This tests whether the 1.000 plateau extends to this neighboring condition and helps define the most robust operating window.

For the final shot, probe whether the strong temperature-induced collapse of the 6–7 pair at 45 C can be offset by a shallower gradient on the best solvent window. It is a last high-information robustness test around the optimum region, while the campaign already retains a max-CRF method if this underperforms.
